key_insight: Text feedback—natural, intermediate supervision richer than scalar rewards but cheaper than full demonstrations—can be used to effectively guide reinforcement learning, improving learning signal quality and scalability.
problem_solved: Addresses the weak informativeness of binary rewards in RL (one bit per rollout) and the high cost of collecting dense demonstrations, by leveraging abundant human-language feedback as a practical middle ground.
method: Collect short human textual critiques or guidance for rollouts instead of only binary labels or full demonstrations.
Train a module that converts text feedback into learning signals (e.g., reward estimates, preference supervision, or policy targets) using LMs or reward models.
Integrate those signals into the RL loop (policy updates, value learning, or supervised distillation) to shape behavior more efficiently.
impact: Enables more informative, scalable supervision for RL agents and LLM fine-tuning by using naturally available text—potentially improving sample efficiency, alignment, and rapid behavior correction without expensive demonstrations.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: rollout -> human text feedback bubble -> text-to-reward/model -> policy update (loop)
Bar or heatmap comparing supervision density: binary reward vs. text feedback vs. demonstrations
Example pair: short textual critique (left) and corrected agent behavior or output (right)
Icons: human annotator, speech/text bubble, reward meter, agent/robot to emphasize human-in-the-loop flow
paper_title: Expanding the Capabilities of Reinforcement Learning via Text Feedback
paper_authors: Yuda Song, Lili Chen, Fahim Tajwar, Remi Munos, Deepak Pathak
